transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-07
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Michael Chen (Redwood AE), Sara López (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (Violet Health), Ethan Cole (Violet Procurement), Lara Mendes (Violet Legal), Jon Park (Violet SRE)

Summary:
Quick procurement/technical preflight ahead of go-to-prod decision. Discussed MSA redlines, DPA expectations, SLA tiers, pricing path for hosted vs dedicated, pilot scope, perf baseline, SSO/KMS, and next steps for legal and procurement. Action items captured.

Topics:
- Legal readiness (MSA/DPA redlines, audit logs, data residency)
- SLA and pricing pathing (hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs private deploy)
- Pilot scope and performance benchmarks (throughput/latency targets)
- Security controls (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM)
- Procurement timeline & approvers

Transcript:
[00:00] Michael Chen: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. Um, so the goal for today is quick preflight — procurement and technical so we can tell finance and legal what we need to land the pilot and, um, hopefully the go‑to‑prod decision. Who wants to kick us off from your side?
[00:20] Priya Raman: Yeah hi, Priya here. Thanks Michael. From platform we're mainly worried about stability and data residency. We're in the middle of a quarterly procurement window, so timing is tight.
[00:34] Ethan Cole: Ethan — procurement. Timeline: we need SOW + pricing and any special egress fees by next Friday ideally. Also need to know if KMS keying will be customer managed.
[00:48] Lara Mendes: And Lara for legal — we'll circulate MSA redlines; main asks are stronger audit logging, rights for incident response, and clarifying data termination and deletion.
[01:05] Sara López: Cool. I'll probably jump in on the technical SLOs and pilot proposal. Quick flag — Redwood's Dedicated offering is often recommended for predictable throughput but you can also do hosted with reserved capacity. There are tradeoffs we should talk through.
[01:24] Jon Park: Jon — SRE. Key numbers: we're targeting 99.95% for API latency under 200ms p95 for the conversational endpoints. Also egress limits matter; network charges could blow the budget.
[01:42] Michael Chen: Good. Let's walk through the legal asks first since that's blocking procurement. Lara, can you say more about the MSA redlines you're planning?
[01:53] Lara Mendes: Sure. The usual: indemnity clarifications, data classification scope — we want to be explicit that PHI-like data isn't shared outside the VPC. Also request for longer log retention for 13 months, and a stronger breach notification SLA of 24 hours.
[02:15] Michael Chen: Understood. We can share our DPA — Redwood's DPA maps to SOC2 controls. We also offer Private deployment option where control plane is in your VPC and keys are customer-managed via KMS/HSM. That should help with the PHI concern.
[02:34] Priya Raman: Private deploy is attractive but that's a heavier lift. How much operational overhead is that? Who patches runtime and who runs capacity?
[02:45] Sara López: For Private, you get autonomy: you host the inference nodes in your environment — our control plane can be customer‑managed; Redwood provides images and an ops runbook. We do a managed support model for security patches on the control plane if you opt-in. There's also a middle ground — Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPUs) in a dedicated tenancy so you still get predictable throughput without full on‑prem.
[03:13] Ethan Cole: From procurement standpoint, cost predictability is key. Can you outline the price difference — ballpark — between hosted per-token pricing vs Dedicated monthly commit?
[03:25] Michael Chen: Yeah ballpark: hosted variable is lowest up to low volume; at our volumes you'd probably pay more per token if you don't commit. Dedicated gives a committed capacity discount — roughly 30–45% off hosted per-token at scale. Exact numbers we'll send in the worksheet.
[03:42] Jon Park: What about quantization and model variants? We want to ensure the model quality doesn't degrade if you switch quantized variants to save cost.
[03:52] Sara López: Great question. We run model-sensitivity evals and can pin a model version. For most workloads we recommend enabling int8 or mixed precision quantization with our Optimize toolkit, but we provide quality regression testing tied to your eval prompts. We'll include that in the pilot scope.
[04:12] Michael Chen: Let's table technical benchmarks for a minute — Lara, does Redwood's standard DPA and SOC2 artifact usually address the log retention and notification ask? If not, what specific redline language are you expecting?
[04:26] Lara Mendes: Typically the DPA covers retention, but we want a guaranteed 13 months for audit logs and a 24-hour initial notification for security incidents, plus a defined escalation path. Also, where encryption at rest and in transit are mentioned, we want confirmation of customer KMS integration.
[04:45] Michael Chen: We have encryption at rest, in transit, and KMS integrations. For the 24-hour notification — our incident response team aims for rapid notification; 24 hours is aggressive but we have customers on tighter timelines and we can look at contract language. We'll follow up with Legal on acceptable SLAs.
[05:02] Priya Raman: Can you send the SOC2 report and the DPA template? We can start internal review.
[05:08] Michael Chen: Absolutely — next steps, we'll drop the SOC2 and DPA. I'll put that action item in.

[05:20] [Checkpoint — switching to pilot scope]
[05:21] Sara López: For pilot I propose: 2-week pilot, start with 1 model endpoint for conversation and 1 for embeddings. We'll run a 1-hour stress run simulating your expected 50k/day profile, capture latency and token cost, and run cold-start & cache-warm tests. That'll validate throughput and cost.
[05:40] Jon Park: 50k/day is our preliminary number; during peaks it could be 80k. We also need prefix caching so prompt windows don't blow up throughput — is prefix caching supported?
[05:52] Sara López: Yes, Redwood's runtime supports prefix/KV cache; we can instrument cache hit rates in the pilot. Also will capture tokenization patterns.
[06:03] Ethan Cole: For the pilot SOW, we need to know billing treatment — trial credits vs invoiced pilot. Also acceptance criteria — what constitutes success to move to reserved capacity.
[06:16] Michael Chen: Typically we do a short eval under a trial credit for an initial baseline — then a paid pilot if you need longer-duration SLA-backed tests. Success criteria we recommend: meet p95 latency under agreed threshold, cost per 1k tokens below target, and no critical security redlines unresolved. We'll draft suggested acceptance criteria in the SOW.
[06:37] Priya Raman: Procurement will need the expected monthly run-rate for the first three months post pilot for budgeting.
[06:45] Michael Chen: We'll model two scenarios: conservative and aggressive usage and include committed pricing bands.

[07:00] [Timestamps and small interruptions — simulating realistic transcription noise]
[07:00] Speaker 1: mm-hmm
[07:03] Sara López: Quick sec — question on egress fees: are you planning to host attachments and binary artifacts in your VPC, or will those be transferred back to Redwood?
[07:15] Priya Raman: We plan to host all PHI attachments in our VPC; inference can happen in a dedicated Redwood pool but we want egress minimized.
[07:25] Sara López: Then Dedicated with a peered VPC or Private deployment are the better fits to reduce egress fees. We'll note peering options in the runbook.

[07:40] Lara Mendes: One more legal note: indemnity and liability caps. We're going to propose carve-outs for regulated data.
[07:50] Michael Chen: Understood. We'll have legal engage.

[08:05] Jon Park: On auth, SSO is required — SAML/SCIM for user provisioning. Also token rotation and least privilege on API keys.
[08:18] Sara López: We support SAML SSO + SCIM, and RBAC in console. API keys can be scoped and rotated; we support customer KMS for private deployments.
[08:30] Ethan Cole: Does Redwood's console support token-level cost breakdown? We need per-team cost visibility for chargeback.
[08:37] Michael Chen: Yes. Redwood Console has token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards. We'll send screenshots.

[09:00] [Mid-call detail: pricing nuance and procurement Qs]
[09:02] Ethan Cole: If we go Dedicated, is there a minimum commit term? 12 months?
[09:08] Michael Chen: We usually do 12-month committed capacity for Dedicated; we can do quarterly review and bump/burn options. There are shorter pilots but with less favorable pricing.
[09:19] Priya Raman: For compliance, does Redwood have any FedRAMP plans? We might need FedRAMP Moderate for some customers.
[09:27] Michael Chen: At the moment we don't have FedRAMP Moderate certified, but we have customers using Private deployments in FedRAMP-suitable environments. We can discuss a path if that becomes a firm requirement.
[09:40] Lara Mendes: Also would like to know data residency options — are there region controls for where inference runs?
[09:46] Sara López: Yes region routing is supported; requests can be pinned to region and we can route by policy. We'll include region mapping.

[10:05] [Noise — speaker overlap, transcription artifacts: "Redwood Dedicate" etc]
[10:05] Speaker 2: yeah
[10:07] Michael Chen: Sorry, said Redwood Dedicate — I mean Dedicated.
[10:10] Priya Raman: Lol, okay noted.

[10:20] Sara López: On the technical side, we need a sample of your production prompts and representative traffic to run the sensitivity and regression tests. Ideally a 24-hour sample.
[10:31] Priya Raman: We'll anonymize and send a 24-hour sample. How do you want that delivered? S3 link?
[10:37] Sara López: S3 link with temporary creds, or we can provide a secure upload endpoint. We'll share the secure upload details in the follow-up.

[10:52] Michael Chen: Quick procurement note: any special billing terms like escrow or extended payment terms we need to know now?
[10:59] Ethan Cole: We prefer Net45 for enterprise; standard Redwood terms are Net30, so this might need Finance sign-off. We'll mark as a negotiation point.
[11:08] Michael Chen: Okay we'll flag that in the SOW.

[11:20] [Deep-dive interlude — performance and inference runtime]
[11:21] Sara López: Performance: our runtime does continuous batching, KV cache management, and can select quantized kernels. For a 200ms p95 target at your payload size we'll propose a mix of batching and warm cache. Cold-starts will be slower; we'll measure those in the bench.
[11:39] Jon Park: Any way to limit cost during cold starts?
[11:42] Sara López: Use warm pools or keep-jobs pinned, or use burst capacity with fallback to smaller models for non-critical paths. Also token caps and truncation policies help.

[12:00] [Security micro-questions]
[12:01] Lara Mendes: Access logs — can we get per-token audit trails for debugging?
[12:07] Sara López: We capture detailed traces and request ids that can be sent to your log destination. We also support audit streaming to your SIEM.
[12:17] Lara Mendes: Good.

[12:25] Michael Chen: Okay let's capture concrete next steps — I'll summarize and then we'll open floor.
[12:31] Michael Chen: Action items: Michael will send SOW + pricing; Sara will run perf baseline and share runbook; Lara will circulate redlines; Priya will confirm budget approvers; Ethan will flag payment-term request. Anything to add?
[12:46] Priya Raman: Please also include a breakdown for cost with and without KV cache savings and an estimate of egress.
[12:55] Michael Chen: Noted — we'll include egress modeling in the worksheet.

[13:05] [Customer quick questions — clarifications]
[13:06] Jon Park: If we decide to go Dedicated, how long does provisioning take?
[13:11] Sara López: Dedicated pools can be provisioned in 7–14 days once contract is signed and payment provisioned; private on‑prem takes longer (weeks to months) depending on infra.
[13:23] Ethan Cole: For audit, can Redwood accept SOC2 onto our vendor portal?
[13:28] Michael Chen: Yes we can. We'll share the SOC2 and typical security pack.

[13:40] [Wrap & recap]
[13:41] Michael Chen: Great. To recap: Redwood will share pricing + SOW + SOC2 + DPA template by EOD Friday. We'll schedule the perf baseline run for next week — Sara will coordinate. Violet will send MSA redlines and a 24-hour anonymized traffic sample. Procurement will confirm budget owners. Legal will review the 24-hour logs retention ask.
[14:05] Lara Mendes: Sounds good. One ask — if you could flag any nonstandard clauses in your MSA that typically cause procurement pushback, that would help us speed review.
[14:14] Michael Chen: Will do. We'll include a short memo of sticky clauses.
[14:20] Priya Raman: Thanks everyone.
[14:22] Michael Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the materials.

[61:00] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcription: speaker labels are approximate; minor transcription errors present (e.g., Redwood Dedicate / KV cash), but content and timestamps reflect the meeting flow.
